A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 24 readable pages, including Appendices A–C. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and proofs without material gaps.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original supervised-learning experiments on perturbed QPLIB instances, with training curves in Figure 4 and training and validation losses in Table 2.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original experiments predicting feasibility, objective values, and optimal solutions, including the outcomes in Figure 4 and Table 2.

M1.justification: The tripartite graph encoding, embedding functions, four message-passing sublayers, readout procedures, and training losses are unchanged. Describing the graph as undirected relocates an existing specification.

E1.justification: Both versions use datasets generated from QPLIB instances 1157, 1493, and 1353 for the same three prediction tasks. The revised mathematical counterexamples are not additional training or evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. IPOPT remains the solver generating training labels. The newly cited NeuralQP framework is not experimentally compared with the proposed GNN.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains 500 training and 100 testing instances per dataset, the same perturbation and convexification procedures, BCE/MSE losses, T = 2, hidden dimension 64, and optimizer settings. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The training-loss analyses are unchanged, and neither version adds ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or error analyses. The revised nonconvex counterexamples belong to the theoretical argument.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both retain the same practice of reporting best training and validation losses.

E6.justification: Figure 4 and every entry in Table 2 are unchanged. For example, QPLIB 1157 validation losses remain 3.53e-2, 9.78e-2, and 8.39e-2 for feasibility, objective value, and solution prediction. Changed analytical counterexample optima are addressed under T1.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces box/sum-constrained counterexamples with unit-ball QCQPs, changing their optima from 1 and 0 to -1/2 and -1 and replacing their solution sets. Appendix C adapts the WL argument from six to twelve quadratic nodes and changes the feasibility threshold from 1/2 to -3/4. These are revised witnesses for unchanged Propositions 1–2; the main convex approximation theorem and its proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: V2 removes the abstract's claim to be the first investigation of GNN representation power for QCQPs and deletes blanket assertions that existing LCQP representations cannot capture quadratic constraints. The proposed representation and principal expressivity claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 adds a coefficient-count complexity rationale and explains limitations of hyperedge representations and variable-dimensional node features. This develops the motivation for the tripartite representation. Interpretations of the experiments and the convex versus nonconvex applicability boundary remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access link, IPOPT labeling procedure, data-generation instructions, network and optimizer hyperparameters, and infinity-indicator disclosure are retained. The latter moves with a footnote without changing its content.

R1.justification: V2 adds NeuralQP by Xiong et al. (2024) to the introduction and references, acknowledging a hypergraph framework for QCQPs. Together with the narrowed novelty wording and discussion of alternative representations, this provides a limited refinement of research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction and Section 2.2 receive focused rewrites, including two explanatory bullets about alternative representations, alongside wording and typo corrections. The overall section and appendix organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The same four figures and two tables are retained, with Figure 3 relocated from page 7 to page 8 and surrounding material reflowed. Figure 3 itself remains unchanged and still displays the earlier constraints despite the replacement of the counterexamples in the text.

improvement.justification: V2 improves contextual precision by acknowledging NeuralQP and narrowing novelty claims. However, the revised counterexamples leave Figure 3 inconsistent with the text, and Appendix C's squared-node update references h1_3 although the constraint color is now h1_4. With the main theorem and empirical evidence unchanged, the contextual gains and introduced inconsistencies in the mathematical exposition do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
